newsitem.title: CHINA: First Sino-foreign trade firms to open soon.
newsitem.headline: First Sino-foreign trade firms to open soon.

text.p: Two joint venture Sino-foreign trade firms, China's first, are due to begin operations soon in Shanghai in a major reform of China's foreign trade system, the Business News said on Friday.

The Dong Ling (Orient-Mitsubishi) Co Ltd and the Lansheng-Daewoo Co Ltd had been approved by Beijing to do foreign trade business in China, making them the first firms with foreign partners permitted to take part in China's foreign trade, the newspaper said.

"The establishment of the two Sino-foreign foreign trade firms indicates the resolution of our government to further open to the outside world and promote the development of China's foreign trade," the newspaper said.

"It will benefit China's efforts to reform its foreign trade sector, introduce international experience in managing foreign trade and increase our country's stake in the international market," it said.
Until economic reforms were launched in the late 1970s, China's foreign trade business was controlled solely by the central government.
Since reforms were introduced, Beijing has gradually allowed local governments and big industrial groups into the sector, but foreign companies have been banned.

President Jiang Zemin promised in October 1995 that Beijing would open foreign trade to foreign firms on a trial basis in Shanghai and other major cities as a further step in China's opening to the outside world.
